title: You’re not too late. You’re being prepared.
paragraphs: You’re not too late. You’re being prepared.
Let that sink in for a moment.

Because one of the quietest fears people carry is this:
“I’m behind.”

Behind in life.
Behind in success.
Behind in purpose.
Behind in where everyone else seems to be.
You scroll through social media and it feels like everyone started the race before you.

Someone already built the business.
Someone already found their calling.
Someone already bought the house.
Someone already got married.
Someone already succeeded.
And there you are…
Standing at the starting line.
Watching the dust of everyone else’s footsteps fade into the distance.
It can make you question everything.
You start asking painful questions in the quiet moments:

“Did I miss my chance?”
“Did I start too late?”
“Did I waste too many years?”
“Did God forget about me?”
But here is a truth that can completely change how you see your life:
God does not measure your life by human timelines.
He measures it by purpose.

The world says:
“If you haven’t made it by now, you’re behind.”

God says:
“I am still writing your story.”

The world says:
“You should have started earlier.”

God says:
“I started preparing you earlier.”

The world says:
“You’re late.”

God says:
“You’re right on time.”
Here’s something powerful many people forget:
God often delays the start so He can strengthen the runner.
David waited years before becoming king.
Joseph spent years in prison before stepping into leadership.
Moses lived 40 years in the wilderness before God called him.
Even Jesus waited 30 years before beginning His public ministry.
Think about that.
The Son of God Himself did not rush His calling.
So why do we believe our timeline must look perfect?
The truth is this:

Sometimes God allows you to feel like the race already started…
so you stop trying to run someone else’s lane.
Because comparison is one of the fastest ways to lose your calling.
When you watch everyone else, you lose focus on the lane God gave you.
And the enemy loves that.
He whispers:

“You’re behind.”
“You’re late.”
“You missed it.”
But heaven says something different.
Heaven says:

“Wait for the Lord; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the Lord!”
— Psalm 27:14
Waiting is not wasted.
Waiting is where God builds endurance.
Waiting is where He shapes your character.
Waiting is where He strengthens the faith you will need when the race gets hard.
The world celebrates speed.
But God values preparation.
Because when your moment finally comes, God doesn’t want you to just start the race…
He wants you ready to finish it.
And that’s why some people start earlier.
But you were being prepared.
Prepared for strength.
Prepared for resilience.
Prepared for purpose.
Prepared for a story that will impact more people than you realize.
Look closely at the image in this poster.
The runner isn’t panicking.
He isn’t quitting.
He isn’t walking away.
He’s doing something powerful.
He’s still at the starting line.
Still focused.
Still determined.
Still believing the race is worth running.
And maybe that’s exactly where you are right now.
You may feel like everyone else is ahead.
But God has not disqualified you.
Your race is not over.
Your lane is still open.
Your story is still unfolding.
The moment you step forward in faith…
everything can change.
Because with God, starting late does not mean finishing last.
Sometimes the runner who starts last finishes strongest.
And one day, you may look back and realize something incredible:
The delay that frustrated you…
was the preparation that saved you.
So if you feel behind in life right now, hear this clearly:

You are not forgotten.
You are not disqualified.
You are not too late.
You are being prepared.
Your race is still ahead.
And when God says go…
no lost time can stop what He planned for your life.

Someone in your life may need this reminder today.
Encourage them.
And if you’re in a season of waiting, I want to ask you something:
What is something you’re trusting God’s timing for right now?
Your story might be the encouragement someone else needs today.
